requirements.name: Universal AI entry
requirements.text: Every supported AI enters through one provider-neutral orientation contract, resolves live Git and project-local authority deterministically, and stops before mutation when exact approval or lane ownership is absent.

requirements.name: Capability- and cost-aware routing
requirements.text: Routing uses capability roles and risk, not mandatory vendor or model names: deterministic tools first, bounded low-cost evidence lanes, one accountable writer, and independent review only when required by risk or gate.

requirements.name: Minute-scale Kanban delivery lifecycle
requirements.text: Work flows through explicit requirement, refinement, implementation, verification, independent review, QA/SIT, Human UAT, release, deployment, hypercare, and Done gates; blocked and awaiting-release states remain visible.

requirements.name: Deterministic local checkpoints
requirements.text: A transition designated as checkpoint-eligible by the approved schema must create exactly one idempotent project-local checkpoint after the authorized transition is accepted and durably recorded; accepted transitions explicitly designated non-checkpointing create none. Rejection, read-only work, tests, support activity, stale or conflicting requests, and replay create no lifecycle checkpoint. A narrative save requires an explicit user command or confirmation, creates a project-local event only, and implies neither a lifecycle transition nor external synchronization.

requirements.name: Fail-closed egress
requirements.text: RAG, vault, hub, network, or other external delivery requires current exact destination-specific human authorization before credentials or event content are read and before any copy or network activity begins. Local event creation remains independently complete.

requirements.name: Privacy-safe public generalization
requirements.text: Only generic contracts, schemas, scripts, tests, and fictional fixtures may enter the public template; private source evidence remains project-local.

requirements.name: Install and upgrade safety
requirements.text: The generalized template must preserve sovereign project data, user-modified files, editor configuration, rollback evidence, and idempotence during clean installation and existing-repository upgrades.

requirements.name: Recursive improvement without self-authorization
requirements.text: Retrospectives may propose protocol improvements and new work items, but no model may approve its own mutation, release, external action, or template promotion.

routing.policy: Choose the least-expensive orchestration-capable parent for the whole task, use deterministic tools before model tokens, delegate each bounded subtask to the least-cost capable role, escalate on evidence or risk, and return all results to the parent for validation and integration.

orchestrator_selection.rule: Select the least-expensive available model that can reliably own planning, authority interpretation, risk decisions, integration, and final accountability for the task as scoped; do not automatically select either the most expensive model or the cheapest model.
inputs: ambiguity and amount of cross-file or cross-repository integration
security, privacy, data, financial, migration, destructive, or external-action risk
required context length and tool competence
available provider/model capabilities, reliability, latency, and cost
orchestrator_selection.fallback: If no available model meets the required parent capability, stop and request a different model or narrower scope rather than silently downgrading.

delegation_loop: The parent decomposes the approved scope into bounded deliverables with acceptance criteria and an authority boundary.
Deterministic tooling handles facts, validation, tests, checksums, and repeatable transformations before a model lane is used.
Each delegable task goes to the least-cost available role that can complete it reliably; support lanes remain read-only unless the exact approval says otherwise.
A delegate escalates ambiguity, repeated failure, scope drift, sensitive data, external action, or material design decisions to the parent or a stronger role.
All delegated evidence and proposed changes return to the accountable parent for integration, deterministic verification, and gate decisions.
No delegate or parent may self-approve a human gate, broaden scope, or infer downstream authority.

stage_one_local_descriptor: A separately authorized local-only operation creates or selects a finalized immutable payload object and records its local object ID, byte size, media/type class, and cryptographic digest without reading any destination credential or initiating transport.

For a newly created event, the deterministic local event writer computes and stores the descriptor as part of the accepted local event operation. For a provider prompt or other dynamic payload, the command first prepares a local immutable preview/descriptor and stops before egress.

The human sees the declared destination, method, payload class, size, digest, expiry, and outward effect and approves that exact descriptor. If no pre-existing immutable descriptor exists, no egress capability can be issued.
stage_two_guard_and_send: The egress guard first reads only approval/policy metadata and the stored descriptor; absent, stale, wrong, expired, revoked, consumed, or mismatched metadata is denied before payload open/read, credential lookup, destination initialization, process spawn, copy, or network.
After metadata authorization passes, the guard opens the payload once, streams and hashes it, and compares it with the approved digest before credential lookup or transport.
A payload digest or size mismatch records denial, consumes or revokes the attempted capability according to policy, and performs no credential lookup, copy, process spawn, or network.

Only after the streamed payload matches may the guard obtain the exact destination credential and invoke the fake or later separately authorized real transport; commit-time expiry, revocation, destination, method, and digest are checked again.
Dynamic or changed content always requires a new local descriptor and new exact approval; content is never inferred to remain authorized.

executor_admission_contract.default: Every absent, unknown, unregistered, expired, revoked, non-attested, or digest-mismatched AI surface/executor is read-only and cannot acquire or consume writer or egress capability.
registration: A separate local human approval registers an exact surface_id, guarded_executor_id, adapter version, guard executable digest, allowed role classes, expiry, and revocation state in the project-local executor registry.
Registration never grants a work-item operation; each writer or egress capability still requires its own exact approval and reservation where applicable.

The authority and egress guards bind every issued capability to the registered identity and recheck registry version, executable digest, expiry, and revocation immediately before reservation, mutation, payload access, credential lookup, or transport.
A provider surface that cannot present the registered guarded-executor attestation remains read-only/advisory even if its model is otherwise capable.
required_negative_evidence: attempt to reuse a capability from another registered surface

risks.description: The approved fallback base is not contained in observed main and could be misrepresented as released template truth.
risks.mitigation: Bind planning to the exact base, keep planning truth distinct from release truth, and require an explicit integration candidate and immutable release SHA.

git merge-base --is-ancestor succeeds from the approved base to the exact release candidate, or the owner accepts documented equivalent supersession evidence
the exact candidate SHA and tree used for all required tests are the SHA and tree proposed for release
a separate release record names the immutable candidate and does not describe a branch name as released truth
required_evidence: exact base, integration candidate, and release-candidate SHAs
risks.residual_risk: The branch may diverge again after the accepted candidate is frozen.
risks.residual_acceptance: Any later divergence requires a new exact release candidate and release gate; branch movement never updates accepted authority automatically.

risks.description: Private Mulligan records or application-specific assumptions could leak into the public template.
risks.mitigation: Use an exact public-code allowlist, runtime-generated fictional fixtures, data-plane exclusions, automated scans, and independent exact-diff privacy review.
closure_conditions: the candidate diff contains only approved code-plane paths

tracked candidate files plus generated install and update artifacts pass private local-only prohibited-token, personal-path, non-public destination, identity, source-fingerprint, and private-ID scans while an explicit allowlist permits legitimate public documentation domains
planning, work items, events, approvals, origin metadata, and source repository history are absent from installer manifests and checksums

the exact public promotion tree and every commit tree/message newly reachable from the public target contain no project-local planning file or private source fingerprint; private planning commits are not ancestors of the promoted commit
fixtures use fictional values and reserved example.invalid destinations
an independent reviewer records no actionable privacy finding without reproducing private literals
required_evidence: public promotion ancestry and newly reachable history scan
risks.residual_risk: Generic wording may still permit semantic inference or a newly introduced identifier may evade a static token list.
risks.residual_acceptance: The owner must accept the residual privacy review; any discovered leak triggers containment, removal, history-remediation assessment, and a new candidate.

risks.description: Provider/model pins could make the entry and routing protocol unusable from another AI surface.
risks.mitigation: Make one provider-free normative contract, capability/cost metadata, thin adapters, and a common cold-start/rejection contract authoritative.
closure_conditions: no named provider or model is required by normative schemas or acceptance logic
at least two materially distinct AI/provider surfaces pass the same cold-start, authority, routing, rejection, retry, and handoff cases
the least-expensive orchestration-capable parent may delegate down, escalate up, and validate returned work without changing authority
a versioned compatibility record distinguishes optional mappings from protocol requirements
required_evidence: static scan for normative model pins
risks.residual_risk: Provider behavior or tool semantics may change after validation.
risks.residual_acceptance: A provider or adapter change invalidates its compatibility evidence and requires revalidation before it is advertised as supported.

risks.description: Automatic save/checkpoint behavior could create duplicate or unauthorized lifecycle records or imply egress authority.
risks.mitigation: Use one transition ledger, stable idempotency keys, atomic durable transition/checkpoint recording, explicit checkpoint eligibility, and a separate egress gate.
closure_conditions: an accepted checkpoint-eligible transition and its checkpoint are one atomic durable operation
retry and replay converge on the same one checkpoint ID
rejected, invalid, unauthorized, stale, conflicting, blocked, read-only, support, test, ordinary-chat, narrative-save, and non-checkpointing transition cases create zero lifecycle checkpoints
concurrent transition attempts produce exactly one accepted transition/checkpoint pair
checkpoint and handoff creation are project-local and never imply external authorization
crash injection before and after the atomic boundary leaves either the old valid state or the single new valid state
risks.residual_risk: Underlying filesystem, operating-system, or storage corruption can violate normal atomicity assumptions.
risks.residual_acceptance: Append-only evidence, corruption detection, verified backups, and fail-closed recovery remain required; corruption never permits inferred continuation.

risks.description: Installer or updater changes could overwrite sovereign project data, user modifications, or editor configuration.
risks.mitigation: Use pinned disposable copies, exhaustive protected-path fixtures, pre/post byte hashes, manifest divergence tests, two-run idempotency, atomic staging, and second-target restore.
closure_conditions: all protected non-propagating path classes are hash-equal before and after install or upgrade
new installation creates only approved code-plane files, blank local stubs, and one controlled ignore block
manifest-diverged files, untracked extensions, editor collisions, unknown versions, malformed records, and injected failures are preserved or fail before source mutation
first and second runs converge without duplicate entries or unexpected change
restore into a second disposable target reproduces the pre-apply Exocortex, editor, and ignore baseline byte-for-byte
no app, browser, credential, provider, network, service, build, deploy, global-home, or live-repository action occurs
risks.residual_risk: An unknown platform behavior or unclassified future user-data path may not be represented by the generic fixtures.
risks.residual_acceptance: Unknown paths default to preserve-and-stop, each live target requires exact preflight and external backup, and no rehearsal authorizes a live rollout.

risks.description: A planning approval could be mistaken for implementation, rehearsal, release, or promotion authority.
risks.mitigation: Keep G1 at refined with no writer, then implement machine-validated one-time approval capabilities bound to an attested registered guarded executor plus exact work item, operation, target path/SHA/destination/content digest, approver, expiry, and reservation.
closure_conditions: missing, planning-only, wrong-item, wrong-operation, wrong-target, wrong-ref, expired, revoked, consumed, or digest-mismatched authority is rejected before reservation, write, child process, credential lookup, content read, copy, or network
a valid capability authorizes only its exact operation and is consumed once
the current writer reservation, target digest, approval digest, expiry, and revocation state are rechecked immediately before commit or transport
read-only and support roles cannot acquire mutation capability
every capability is bound to a registered surface_id, guarded_executor_id, adapter version, guard executable digest, registry version, expiry, and revocation state

missing, unregistered, non-attested, wrong-executor, wrong-adapter, digest-mismatched, expired, revoked, or cross-surface capability use is rejected before reservation, mutation, payload access, credential lookup, or transport

every shipped command, skill, hook, and provider adapter loads the canonical gate; an AI surface with unmediated filesystem or network tools that cannot be constrained to the registered guarded executor is classified read-only/advisory and cannot be an approved writer or egress actor
an independent reviewer verifies fail-closed ordering and no implicit downstream authority
required_evidence: negative matrix covering every mismatch and replay
executor-registry and guarded-executor attestation negative matrix
one valid one-time positive case using only a disposable target
risks.residual_risk: A human can still approve the wrong bounded action, and an unmanaged AI/host tool outside the guarded execution boundary can ignore repository protocol.
risks.residual_acceptance: Every approval prompt displays the exact action, target, outward effect, expiry, rollback, and excluded next gates. Only surfaces technically constrained to the guarded path may receive writer/egress roles; other surfaces remain read-only/advisory, and the human remains the non-delegable acceptance boundary.

risks.description: A moving, incomplete, or tampered template source could pass informal review and alter an installed target.
risks.mitigation: Pin the exact local candidate commit and tree, verify every executable surface and expected file against SHA256SUMS, and reject missing, extra, or mismatched entries before target mutation.
closure_conditions: installation and rehearsal accept an exact pinned candidate rather than implicit moving main
every user-executable code-plane surface is covered by the integrity manifest
missing, extra, modified, or unhashed executable fixtures fail before creating a target delta
provenance evidence records candidate commit, tree, integrity-manifest hash, and offline source
required_evidence: missing, extra, and mismatch negative tests
risks.residual_risk: A compromised trusted local root could falsify both files and their local manifest.
risks.residual_acceptance: Promotion requires an independently reviewed exact Git object and trusted publication channel; live consumers must pin the accepted artifact digest.

risks.description: Concurrency or time-of-check/time-of-use changes could let stale writers, approvals, or destinations act after validation.
risks.mitigation: Use atomic compare-and-swap reservations, versioned state, stable idempotency keys, revocation records, and commit-time target/authority digest checks.
closure_conditions: 32 concurrent attempts for reservation, transition, checkpoint, approval consumption, and revocation yield exactly one valid winner where one is permitted
losers create no partial state and stale lease holders cannot commit
changing approval, target, destination, content digest, expiry, or revocation between initial check and commit causes rejection
retry after conflict converges without duplicate checkpoint or handoff
risks.residual_risk: Pathological storage or locking behavior may exceed the tested concurrency model.
risks.residual_acceptance: Unsupported atomic primitives fail closed; storage platforms must be qualified before use and ambiguous state requires human-led recovery.

risks.description: Legacy, malformed, duplicate, or future-version work-item state could be silently misread or destructively migrated.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit version detection, staged generic legacy-v0 to normalized-v1 to public-v2 migration, backup-first atomic replacement, validation, idempotency, and unknown-version refusal.
closure_conditions: blank, valid legacy-v0, valid normalized-v1, current public-v2, unknown, malformed, duplicate-ID, and future-version fixtures have explicit deterministic outcomes
new installs create blank public-v2 local state and do not import history
orientation may read supported legacy state, but mutation requires a separate target-specific migration approval
migration is backup-first, staged, validated, atomic, reversible in a disposable target, and idempotent
private Mulligan records are not committed test fixtures or automatic migration input

risks.residual_risk: A repository may contain a bespoke private legacy extension not represented by the public compatibility matrix.
risks.residual_acceptance: Unrecognized extensions are preserved and mutation stops; a separate project-local migration work item is required.

risks.description: An indirect command, hook, subprocess, memory helper, hub copy, key check, telemetry-like helper, or retry could bypass the visible external-sync gate.
risks.mitigation: Route every outward-capable path through one auditable egress guard and statically reject direct transport bypasses outside that seam.
closure_conditions: direct sync, narrative save, daily/weekly/monthly review, interrupt capture, hub post, key validation, memory-model calls, automatic hooks, subprocess adapters, and retries all use the same guard
all installed command and skill entrypoints load the canonical entry/authority contract before any mutation or outward-capable instruction
absent, expired, wrong-destination, wrong-method, wrong-content-digest, revoked, or consumed authority produces only authorization_denied
denial occurs before credential lookup, event or prompt-content read, destination initialization, process spawn, copy, or network attempt
a fake positive transport receives only the exact authorized destination, operation, and content digest
static scanning fails on curl, urllib, ssh, scp, external copy, or equivalent transport outside the approved guard seam
risks.residual_risk: A future executable or operating-system integration could introduce a new outward mechanism after the inventory is frozen.
risks.residual_acceptance: New executable surfaces require integrity-manifest and egress-inventory updates; unknown outward mechanisms fail CI and cannot be promoted.

risks.description: A green test run could provide false confidence through skipped cases, undiscovered tests, inert mocks, weak assertions, or correlated model review.
risks.mitigation: Use a machine-readable required-case plan, evidence verifier, ordered audit fakes, mutation sensitivity checks, and sterile independent cross-provider UAT.
closure_conditions: every required case ID is discovered, executed, asserted, and represented in the evidence manifest with zero skip
removing the authority, atomicity, protected-path, and checksum safeguards makes the corresponding tests fail
fake transports and child-process shims record ordered calls so a never-called mock cannot silently pass
two distinct AI/provider surfaces orient from repository state without shared conversation context and independently perform the required read-only UAT
deterministic evidence and independent review agree on the exact candidate
risks.residual_risk: Tests and reviewers can still share an unmodeled assumption about real-world behavior.
risks.residual_acceptance: Rehearsals remain disposable, hypercare is mandatory, and any field divergence creates a new corrective work item rather than being waived.

risks.description: Failure after backup, during staging, around atomic replacement, after egress authorization, or during retry could leave partial state or allow delayed unauthorized action.
risks.mitigation: Inject failures at every side-effect boundary, revoke outstanding capabilities and retries, contain the candidate, preserve local evidence, and prove second-target recovery.
closure_conditions: failure after backup, during staging, immediately before atomic replace, after authorization before fake transport, and during retry leaves the original valid or the single new valid state
revocation prevents every queued or replayed transport after the injected failure
local records remain intact and the candidate enters an explicit contained or blocked state
restore into a second disposable target matches the pre-apply baseline byte-for-byte
resumption requires a new approval and fresh evidence rather than reuse of the failed capability
risks.residual_risk: A backup or underlying device may itself be corrupt or unavailable.
risks.residual_acceptance: Backups are verified before mutation, live rollout requires an external recovery copy under its own authority, and unverifiable recovery blocks the rollout.
